message.content:
Here’s a mix of classics, cult favorites, and recent chills—perfect for turning your Friday into a full‑on scream fest:

| # | Title & Year | Why It Works |
|---|--------------|-------------|
| **1** | *Halloween* (1978) – Director John Carpenter introduced Michael Myers as the ultimate “slasher” icon. Its low‑budget suspense turns ordinary suburban nights into nerve‑wracking terror; great for a quick scare before dinner. |
| **2** | *Hereditary* (2018) – A slow‑burn psychological nightmare that builds dread through family secrets and supernatural dread. Ideal when you want something that lingers long after the credits roll. |
| **3** | *It Follows* (2014) – An inventive take on possession horror where the threat follows relentlessly. Perfect for late‑night binge‑watching because its creeping tension keeps everyone glued to the screen. |
| **4** | *A Quiet Place* (2018) – Silence becomes survival. The film’s tense atmosphere makes even mundane sounds feel like potential death throats—a fun way to test how quiet your living room really gets at midnight. |
| **5** | *Midsommar* (2019) – If daylight scares work better than darkness, this sunlit Swedish festival will do. Its unsettling folk rituals make for a unique twist on traditional horror tropes. |
| **6** | *Get Out* (2017) – Combines social satire with genuine jump‑scares. Great conversation starter afterward—and the clever pacing means you’ll stay alert all evening. |
| **7** | *The Conjuring* (2013) – For those who love classic haunted house vibes, Ed and Lorraine Warren bring real‑world paranormal investigations to life. Their grounded storytelling gives a satisfying blend of creepiness and catharsis. |

Feel free to pick one based on mood—whether you’re craving pure gore, mind‑bending dread, or atmospheric chill. Happy haunting!
